messages:
ida: paging: seeing repeated 401->200 sequences from ~12 distinct IPs hitting /v1/internal/sessions/validate. pattern looks like token replay rather than credential stuffing. noticed same truncated token suffix in logs.
ops-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty incident INC-2026-421 triggered by auth-alerts — oncall: marine (oncall).
marine (oncall): acked. pulling traces now. any evidence of data exfil?
ida: no obvious data download yet, just auth validation endpoints. but one req shows a downstream fetch to /keys/lookup (internal) before failing — suspicious.
raj: can you paste the redacted log line? mask token chars.
ida: sure —
ida: ```
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] svc=auth-proxy src=52.23.11.9 path=/v1/internal/sessions/validate hdr=Authorization: Bearer ******abc123def
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] action=kv_lookup key_id=k-user-17 svc=kv-store status=200
```
security-sre: that kv lookup is interesting — keys service should be internal-only. how is proxy getting access?
ben: I see a surge of similar requests from cloudfront edge nodes — likely replaying cached request bodies. IPs don't map to our fleet.
katie: confirmed: logs show a few requests that passed org-id header which should be stripped by our ingress. looks like an older deploy might have not applied header-sanitizer.
marine (oncall): timeline: last deploy to auth-proxy at 2026-03-15T08:50. rolling back that deploy now.
ops-bot: deploy-automation: rollback auth-proxy v2026.03.15-0818 initiated by @marine.
ida: rolling back. also adding temporary WAF rule to block requests with Authorization header pattern ending in "abc123def".
raj: start immediate key rotation for sessions signing key K-auth-sessions? we should consider short-lived revocation if leak confirmed.
security-sre: agree. plan: 1) block suspicious IPs & WAF rule 2) rollback faulty proxy 3) rotate session-signing key (K-auth-sessions-v2) 4) revoke active sessions issued in last 48h by issuing revocation list 5) customer comms draft.
ben: kicking off key rotation now — generating new key in KMS and creating new signing key version. ETA ~15m.
katie: I'll prepare support ticket template and surface to account teams for customers with elevated activity.
marine (oncall): who's owning session revocation script? I can run a targeted revocation for sessions that touched /keys/lookup.
ida: I'll grep traces and build a session-id list, pushing to S3://rbw-temp/revocations-177353. then run revoke script.
security-sre: do not upload PII. redact emails in the list. confirm before revocation.
ben: new key ready. updating auth service to sign with K-auth-sessions-v2 and enabling dual verification for 10m to allow graceful rotation.
ops-bot: deploy-automation: auth-service config updated to use K-auth-sessions-v2.
ida: revocation list assembled (redacted). starting revoke run: `./scripts/revoke_sessions --src s3://rbw-temp/revocations-177353 --dry-run=false`
ida: revoke run completed — 4,312 sessions revoked. most belong to internal-testing and a handful customer IDs flagged.
katie: opening support ticket SUP-7892 to notify affected customers with recommended next steps (sign-out, re-auth). draft in #support-drafts, please review.
security-sre: request legal review for possible exposure of tokens to external IPs. cc @legal. also preserve logs for forensic analysis (increase retention).
raj: network team: please BGP-blackhole the worst offenders and add to denylist.
ops-bot: netops-bot: applied denylist for 52.23.11.0/24 and 34.198.0.0/16 as temporary mitigations.
marine (oncall): handoff: I'm on for next 30m then offshift. @raj please take ownership for post-mortem actions (forensic log collection, KMS audit, review deploy pipeline sanitize step).
raj: taking ownership. compiling timeline + affected customer list.
inc-bot: Incident INC-2026-421 updated: Severity=high, status=mitigated, summary=Auth-proxy rollback + key rotation performed, sessions revoked.
ida: quick note for postmortem: investigate why header-sanitizer config didn't apply on 2026-03-15 deploy — suspect CI race where config file read failed.
katie: comms plan: initial notification to affected customers within 2 hours, follow-up with root cause and mitigations in 72 hours. legal review pending.
security-sre: next steps: forensic handoff to security team, ensure KMS access logs reviewed, rotate any auxiliary keys that had pull access to signing key, review CI for config race conditions.
raj: acknowledged — will own postmortem doc and share draft in #incidents-postmortems.
marine (oncall): thanks all. leaving note: if anything new surfaces ping me directly.
ida: closing slack thread for active coordination, will reopen if we see replay resumed. :white_check_mark:
